sentences.text: 1 This claim petition is filed by the petitioners under Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the death of Sagar H.S. caused in a road traffic accident.

2. The facts leading to the filing of top noted petition are that on 2-10-2018 at about 9.15 a.m. when the petitioner was riding his scooter bearing reg.No.KA-05-HR- 6949 at Quatrand circle,
Shivajinagar, Bengaluru city, at that time, rider of the motor cycle bearing reg.No.TN-10-AC- 1118 came with high rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner, due to impact,
petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries and took treatment at hospital.
The petitioner was working as an Accountant at Private firm and earning Rs.10,000/-p.m. and due to accidental injuries, petitioner lost the income.
Hence prays to award compensation of Rs.15 lakhs from the respondents.
3. After service of notice to respondents, the respondent No.2 remained absent and placed exparte.

respondent No.1 appeared through counsel before this Tribunal and filed written statement wherein contended that this respondent issued a policy to the motor cycle bearing reg.No.TN-10-AC-1118 vide policy bearing No.39010231176203476453 valid from 17-11-2017 to 16- 11-2018.
Both riders of the vehicles in question were not possessing valid and effective driving licence to drive their respective vehicles.
The owners of the vehicles knowing fully entrusted to drive the above said vehicles, who does not possessed valid and effective driving licence to drive his vehicle.
The petition is bad for non compliance of 158(b) and 134(c) of the MV Act.
The alleged accident was occurred on 2-10-2018, the complaint was lodged on 6-10- 2018, there is four days delay in lodging the complaint.

That there is no negligence on the part of the motor cycle bearing reg.No.TN-10-AC-1118,
the same was falsely implicated to get unlawful gain.
The rider of the motor cycle bearing No.TN-10-AC-1118, rode the said endanger human life and dashed against the petitioner.
There is no nexus between the injuries sustained to the petitioner in the alleged accident.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive and highly exorbitant.
Hence prays to dismiss the petition.

4. During the pendency of the trial, the petitioner Kashinath J. was reported to dead and his LR,
Manjula Kashinath/wife was brought on record and she herself examined as PW-1.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings this tribunal has framed the following issues :
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that Kashinath J S/o S.R. Janaji Rao has sustained grievous injuries in an accidnet that was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of the motor cycle bearing reg.No.TN-10-AC-1118 on 2-10-2018 at about 9.15 a.m. at quatrand circle, Shivajinagar, Bengaluru?
2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for?

If so, at what rate? from whom?
3) What order or award?

complaint, spot mahazar, rough sketch, wound certificate, IMV report, charge sheet,
discharge summaries, death certificate, aadhaar card, identity card, medical bills.

During the pendency of the petition, the petitioner was reported to be dead and the LR/wife of the petitioner was brought on record.

It was argued by the learned counsel for the respondent No.1 that there was no nexus between the death and the injuries sustained by the deceased in the accident and the petitioner has died due to his old age and no post mortem was conducted and no charge sheet for 304A was filed and hence the LR of the petitioner cannot claim the compensation and is not entitle for the compensation and prays to dismiss the petition as not maintainable.

On the other hand learned counsel for the petitioner argued that though there is no nexus between the death and injuries sustained by the petitioner in the alleged accident, but LR of the petitioner i.e., petitioner No.1(a) wife of the deceased petitioner is duly entitle for claiming the compensation as petition was filed by the petitioner himself and during the pendency of the petition, the petitioner was died.
In support of her contention, petitioner relied on the decisions reported in-Miscl.First Appeal No.201100 of 2017 (MV-D)-Chandrakanth and Ors Vs Mohd.Yusuf and Ors- 6.
Section 166(5) was inserted by an Act No.32 of 2019 and reads as follows:

"(5) Notwithstanding anything in this Act or any other law for the time being in force,
the right of a person to claim compensation for injury in an accident shall, upon the death of the person injured, survive to his legal representatives, irrespective of whether the cause of death is relatable to or had any nexus with the injury or not."

sentences.text: As could be seen from (5), the sub Section starts with a non obstante clause and declares that the right of a person to claim compensation for injuries sustained by him in an accident would survive to his legal representatives upon his death, even if the death was not relatable to the injuries suffered by him.

8. In other words, by virtue of this amendment, the normal rule that damages for personal injury would come to an end on the death of the injured has been altered completely and the law now permits the legal representatives of the injured to make a claim in respect of the injuries suffered by the injured even after his death.

9. The entitlement of the legal representatives to claim compensation for injuries suffered by the injured has been made explicit under Section 166(5) of the Act and therefore the death of an injured would not result in the claim coming to an end under the provisions of the Motor NC: 2024:KHC- K:6176 Vehicle Act and the legal heirs of the injured can continue to prosecute the claim.

10. The reliance placed on by the learned counsel for the insurer on Kannamma's case i.e., Full Bench can have no application since it was rendered in the year 1990 prior to insertion of Section 166(5) of the Act.

11. The reliance placed on by the learned counsel on the judgment rendered by the Hon'ble Apex Court in AIR 2021 SC 3913, can also be of no avail since the Apex Court in that case did not consider the import of Section 166(5) and the Apex Court was re-iterating the normal proposition of law.

If the Hon'ble Apex Court has not considered Section 166(5) in the said judgment, it cannot be held that it has been decided by the Hon'ble Apex Court with reference to Section 166(5) that the legal representatives of injured cannot continue the proceedings in respect of a claim for compensation for the injuries suffered in a motor vehicle accident.
12.

Since in the instant case, the injured himself had initiated the claim proceedings and the same was continued on his death, by his legal representatives, the provisions of Section 166(5) would automatically be attracted and they would be entitled to continue the proceedings and claim the compensation which was due to the injured.
The finding of the Tribunal to the contrary and its dismissal cannot therefore be sustained.

13. Though in the normal circumstances, the matter would have been remitted to the Tribunal for consideration of the compensation payable, having regard to the fact that the accident is of the year 2011 and 13 years have elapsed, it would be unfair to the parties for a fresh round of litigation and hence it deemed appropriate to determine the compensation payable in this appeal itself.

11. Hon'ble Apex court determining compensation under permanent disability and awarded compensation under the head loss of future income, nourishment, conveyance, attendant and medical bills and loss of amenities along with 6% p.a. interest.

12. Further relied on Civil Appeal No.4800 of 2021- The oriental insurance company limited Vs Kahlon(Deceased) through his legal representative Narinder Kahlon Gosakan and Ors.

sentences.text: The injuries suffered by the deceased in the accident required prolonged hospitalization for six months.
The extent of disability suffered was assessed on 16.06.2000 as 100%.
The extent of disability, pursuant to physiotherapy was reassessed as 75% on 08.08.2002.
In the interregnum, the injured resigned his job on 30.09.2001 at the age of 53 years as he found movement difficult and inconvenient without an attendant as distinct from complete immobility.
The injured was possessing professional qualifications in labour laws and Industrial relations along with a Diploma in Personnel Management.

He may have had to suffer some handicap in also practicing before the labour court, but cannot be held to have suffered 100% physical disability as his capacity for rendering advisory and other work coupled with movement on a wheel chair with the aid of an attendant could still facilitate a reduced earning capacity.
It cannot be held that the injured was completely left with no source of livelihood except to deplete his estate.
In assessing, what has been described as a 'Just Compensation' under the Act, all factors including possibilities have to be kept in mind.
18. The Tribunal, on technicalities rejected his claim for salary, medical expenses and percentage of disability and granted a measly compensation of Rupees one lakh only by a cryptic order.

We are,
therefore, of the opinion that while the claim for personal injuries may not have survived after the death of the injured unrelated to the accident or injuries, during the pendency of the appeal, but the claims for loss of estate caused was available to and could be pursued by the legal representatives of the deceased in the appeal.
19. In Parminder Singh (supra) compensation on the basis of complete loss of income, the percentage of disability, future prospects were granted applying the relevant multiplier.
Again, in Kajal (supra) the injured was assessed as 100 per cent disabled, considering all of which compensation was awarded on the notional future prospects along with relevant multiplier.
The loss of income to the injured in the facts of the present case has to be assessed at 75%.
In view of Raj Kumar (supra) there shall be no deduction towards personal expenses.

20. We see no reason to deviate from the consistent judicial view taken by more than one High Court that loss of estate would include expenditure on medicines, treatment, diet, attendant,
Doctor's fee, etc. including income and future prospects which would have caused reasonable accretion to the estate but for the sudden expenditure which had to be met from and depleted the estate of the injured, subsequently deceased.
21. However, the compensation under the head pain and suffering being personal injuries is held to be unsustainable and is disallowed.
The High Court has not awarded anything towards medical expenses despite hospitalization for six months being an admitted fact.
We therefore award a sum of Rs.1,00,000/ towards medical expenses.

Hence, the reassessed total compensation would be Rs.28,42,175/, calculated hereunder:
13.

In view of the ratios held by the Hon'ble Apex court, this court of the opinion that in the present case, though admittedly there is no nexus between the death and injuries sustained by the petitioner in the alleged accident but it is not in dispute that petitioner has sustained the injuries due to the alleged accident and petitioner Kashinath.J vs National Ins Co Ltd on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28577566/
5 himself has filed present petition during his life time and it is also not disputed that petitioner No.1(a) is the wife of the deceased petitioner.

sentences.text: Hence in view of the principles laid down in the above said decisions, the LR of the petitioner i.e., wife of the petitioner is duly entitle to claim the compensation and the present petition is duly maintainable.
Further as per the above said decision, the LR/wife of the petitioner is entitle to loss of income due to disability under loss of estate.

14. The learned counsel for the respondent No.1 contended that both riders of the motor vehicle is not possessing valid and effective Driving Licence and owner of the offending vehicle knowing fully entrusted to drive the above said vehicle and as such there is a violation of the terms and conditions.

Further respondent No.1 disputed that the alleged accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the petitioner himself and due to the rash and negligent act himself, petitioner has sustained injuries.
15.

In this regard, on perusal of the evidence and materials on record, wife of the petitioner has lodged the complaint on 6-10-2018 against the driver of the motor cycle bearing No.TN-10-AC-1118 as per Ex-P1 wherein she stated that as her husband petitioner was not in a condition to speak and discuss regarding the accident soon after the accident and she was with the petitioner, looking after him in the hospital.
There was a delay in filing the complaint.

Thereafter Shivajinagar traffic police lodged FIR as per Ex- P1, thereafter jurisdictional police conducted a thorough and detailed investigation and filed charge sheet as per Ex- P8 by holding that on 2-10-2018 at about 9.15 a.m.
when petitioner was proceeding from Taz circle and turning towards Toppada Modaliyar road, right turn, at that time, rider of the motor cycle No.KA-05-HR-6949 rode his motor cycle from Taz circle towards Septings road in high speed, rash and negligent manner and hit to the vehicle of the petitioner who was proceeding in front of him from Taz circle towards Septings road while taking right turn, as a result of which petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
16.

Apart from this, on perusal of the Ex-P5 the wound certificate, ti is clearly stated that RTA on two wheeler and hit by another two wheeler on 2-10-2018 and he was immediately taken to the hospital at 9.55 a.m.

on perusal of Ex-P4 sketch it clearly shows that the spot of accident is a junction and accident has been taken place in the middle of the road, both motor vehicles were moving in the same direction, petitioner was moving towards Toppada Modaliyar road by turning his motor cycle towards the right, at that time, the driver of the offending vehicle came in the same direction and hit to the petitioner.
Admittedly the spot of accident is a junction, at that place the rider of the vehicles must be drive carefully and slowly.

If the driver of the offending vehicle bearing reg.No.TN-10-AC-1118 would have drove his motor cycle slowly, after looking into the vehicles at the junction, certainly the accident would not have been taken place.
Thus Ex-P3 and Ex-P4 clearly shows that accident has been taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle.

Respondent has not lead evidence of rider of offending vehicle and disproved evidence of PW-1 nor there are no other evidence and materials on record to held that charge sheet is collusive and defective.

sentences.text: At this juncture, It is necessary to apply the citation reported in AIR 2011 SC 1504 between Parmeshwari -vs- Amir Chand & Ors - wherein it has been held that - "In a situation of this nature, the Tribunal has rightly taken a holistic view of the matter.
It was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied."
18. Thus, the oral evidence of PW-1 discussed with the above documentary evidence are sufficient for the purpose of the actionable claim under the Motor Vehicles Act.
Mere taking of defence is not sufficient to dislodge the testimony of other side, which has no sanctity in the eyes of Law.
19. Under such circumstances the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
Consequently I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the driver of offending vehicle.

20. In addenda, in a claim for compensation u/s 166 of M.V Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in 'MANGALA RAM VS. ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY reported in (2018) 5 SCC 656.

sentences.text:
With this observation issue No.1 is answered as 'In the Affirmative'.
21. ISSUE NO.2:
As already discussed above the petitioner has proved that the accident took place due to the actionable negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Therefore the LR of the petitioner/wife of the deceased petitioner is entitled for compensation.
22. AGE, AVOCATION AND INCOME:
So far as the age of petitioner/ is concerned, the petitioner contended that at the time of accident he was aged 70 years.
From the Ex-P12-Aadhaar card it reveals that petitioner's year of birth is 1949.
Hence as on the date of accident i.e.,2018, petitioner was aged about 69 years.

With regard to the income, the deceased petitioner contended that he was working as Accountant at private firm, Bangalore and drawing salary of Rs.10,000/- per month at the time of accident and due to accidental injuries, he is suffering from permanent disability and deformity.
The deceased petitioner has not produced any documentary or oral evidence to prove his avocation and income.
Therefore, the income of the petitioner has to be taken into consideration as notional income.
In the absence of proof taking into consideration the date of accident, age of the petitioner and nature of her work, if his income is assessed at Rs.12,500/- p.m, it would meet the ends of justice.
23. LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY:- The petitioner 1(a) has not adduced any evidence of the doctor to prove the disability suffered by the deceased petitioner.
In absence of evidence about any disability, this court cannot grant any compensation under the head loss of future income due to disability to the original claimant i.e., deceased petitioner.

sentences.text: PAIN & SUFFERINGS :
The compensation under the head pain and sufferings being personal injuries and personal in nature is held to be unsustainable.
25. ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES:

Admittedly as per the materials available on record, petitioner is a resident of St.John road, near Solar automobiles, Shivan Chetty Garden, Bangalore north and took treatment as inpatient at Hosmat hospital from 2-10- 2018 to 4-10-2018, from 7-3-2019 to 8-3-2019 and from 14-3-2019 to 18-3-2019 total for a period of 10 days and certainly he would have hired the cab for traveling to the hospital and underwent right humerous ORIF with bicondylar plating on 3-10-2018, planned for right distal humerus reosteosynthesis with bone graft, removal of implant and re-osteosynthesis of right distal humerus done on 15-3-2019 with dorsolateral LCP and recon plate.

and certainly, it cannot be disputed that petitioner is dependent on the others and during the course of her treatment the petitioner might have spent more amount towards attendant charges, conveyance, extra nutritious food etc.

Hence a sum of Rs.15,000/-
under this head.
26. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:

Due to injuries suffered by petitioner,
petitioner would obviously have faced depression, anxiety, disappointment & frustration and also suffer discomfort in enjoying the normal pleasures & joys of human life till his death.
Hence a sum of Rs.25,000/- is awarded under this head.
27. MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The petitioner has produced Ex-P16-medical bills for Rs.22,640/- to prove the expenditure towards treatment taken by her.

Upon considering the above bills and injuries sustained by the petitioner in the accident, the resultant disability suffered by him due to such injuries, I proceed to award Rs.22,640/- under the head of medical expenses.

28. The calculation table stands as follows :
1 Attendant charges, extra 15,000/-
 nutritious food and  conveyance charges  2 Loss of future amenities and 25,000/-
 happiness  3 Medical expenses 22,640/-
 Total 62,640/-

In assessing, what has been described as a 'Just Compensation' under the Act, all factors including possibilities have to be kept in mind.
We are,
therefore, of the opinion that while the claim for personal injuries may not have survived after the death of the injured unrelated to the accident or injuries, during the pendency of the appeal, but the claims for loss of estate caused was available to and could be pursued by the legal representatives of the deceased in the appeal.
In view of the ratios held by the Hon'ble Apex court, this court of the opinion that in the present case, though admittedly there is no nexus between the death and injuries sustained by the petitioner in the alleged accident but it is not in dispute that petitioner has sustained the injuries due to the alleged accident and petitioner Kashinath.J vs National Ins Co Ltd on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28577566/
5 himself has filed present petition during his life time and it is also not disputed that petitioner No.1(a) is the wife of the deceased petitioner.
Mere taking of defence is not sufficient to dislodge the testimony of other side, which has no sanctity in the eyes of Law.
Consequently I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the driver of offending vehicle.
20. In addenda, in a claim for compensation u/s 166 of M.V Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in 'MANGALA RAM VS. ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY reported in (2018) 5 SCC 656.
The deceased petitioner has not produced any documentary or oral evidence to prove his avocation and income.
Therefore, the income of the petitioner has to be taken into consideration as notional income.
In the absence of proof taking into consideration the date of accident, age of the petitioner and nature of her work, if his income is assessed at Rs.12,500/- p.m, it would meet the ends of justice.
23. LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY:- The petitioner 1(a) has not adduced any evidence of the doctor to prove the disability suffered by the deceased petitioner.
In absence of evidence about any disability, this court cannot grant any compensation under the head loss of future income due to disability to the original claimant i.e., deceased petitioner.
